artworks.title: Vertumnus and Pomona
artworks.description: Pontormo's orchard goddess at Poggio a Caiano — Pomona as Renaissance abundance under the Medici villa vault.

artworks.title: Vertumnus and Pomona
artworks.description: Melzi's Berlin panel shows Vertumnus in crone disguise wooing Pomona among fruit and foliage — Leonardo's pupil turning Ovid's orchard courtship into Lombard grace. Gemäldegalerie, Berlin.

artworks.title: Vertumnus and Pomona
artworks.description: Rubens' oil for the Torre de la Parada cycle stages the god's final unveiling: Vertumnus sheds the old-woman mask before Pomona. Flemish abundance for the Roman fruit-tree goddess.

artworks.title: Landscape with Vertumnus and Pomona
artworks.description: Bloemaert nests the orchard courtship in a Dutch world landscape — Pomona listening as the disguised Vertumnus persuades. Yale University Art Gallery.

artworks.title: Vertumnus and Pomona
artworks.description: Eeckhout, Rembrandt's pupil, paints Pomona half-turned toward the god's disguise — soft Dutch light on Ovid's autumn romance. Google Art Project scan of the orchard pair.

popCulture.title: Pomona
popCulture.description: Roman goddess of fruit trees — still the name for orchards, autumn, and places that claim her abundance.
